text:
arjun: quick heads-up — ran a small bring-up for hybrid early-fallthrough on llama3-12b-4bit.
liz: nice. what's the config? single-GPU or multi?
arjun: single 80GB A100. runtime flag: --spec-fallthrough=hybrid --early-threshold=0.18
rob: how are you measuring quality? simple prompt-suite or eval harness?
arjun: evalset: evalset-small-v2 (1k instruction+QA pairs). metrics: exact-match, accept-rate, and a tiny perplexity check.
maya: any regressions vs 16-bit baseline?
arjun: minor drop in exact-match ~0.9% absolute. accept-rate unchanged. p95 latency down from 210ms -> 145ms on short prompts.
liz: that's promising for latency. does cost per-token improve too?
arjun: yes, token throughput +38% in steady state with continuous batching on the single GPU run.
rob: can you paste the command and the metric snippet?
arjun: ```
# run harness
python run_eval.py --model llama3-12b-4bit --spec-mode hybrid --early-threshold 0.18 --batch 8 --dataset evalset-small-v2
```
arjun: metrics snippet:
```
exact_match: 78.6 -> 77.7 (-0.9)
accept_rate: 92.1 -> 92.0 (-0.1)
p95_latency_ms: 210 -> 145
throughput_tok/s: 4200 -> 5780
```
maya: did you run with kv-cache warmup? speculative prefetched tokens can skew perf.
arjun: yes warmed with prefix warmup=16, and we disabled speculative prefetching for the baseline run to keep it comparable.
liz: any weird failure modes? hallucination rate change?
arjun: spot checks show slightly more numeric rounding errors on long arithmetic prompts — looks quantization-y not speculative.
rob: could that be from blocked attention or early termination bias? Might need a tiny beam or temperature tweak in the spec path.
arjun: good call. next run: same config + spec-temp=0.8 and fallback-beam=2.
ops-bot: canary started on eng-ml-canary-3 with model=llama3-12b-4bit, flags=[spec-fallthrough=hybrid, early-threshold=0.18]
liz: can you add a randomized seed sweep? early threshold might be brittle at 0.18.
arjun: will sweep [0.12,0.15,0.18,0.22], each 200 examples. planning to log per-prompt deltas and push to shared spreadsheet.
maya: when you push results, add a column for "regression_count >5%" so we can gate rollout.
rob: also capture latency tail per-route (short vs long prompts) — fallback penalties matter only for short.
arjun: agreed. next update in ~3hrs after the sweep. tagging @liz @rob for quick look when done. :thumbsup:
